paragraphs.notes: The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. This paragraph is the tail of a very long alphabetical list of herbicide common names and development codes that begins on earlier pages; it opens mid-list with 'oryzalin' and carries no paragraph number, as WO publications of this vintage do not number paragraphs. Almost every token is a common name or a company code rather than German prose; only the connectives 'und dessen Ester', 'und deren Esterderivate', 'z.B.', 'd.h.' and 'und' are German, and only those plus the German chemical spellings have been changed in the en field. Systematic names are anglicised in en (Chlor to chloro, fluor to fluoro, propansaeure to propanoic acid, -methylester to methyl ester, indazol to indazole, triazol-1-carboxamid to triazole-1-carboxamide, tetrazol to tetrazole); the ring locants, brackets and hyphens are left exactly as printed. Printed as-is and not normalised: 'trifluor-methyl' is hyphenated in the SN 106279 entry but 'trifluormethyl' is unhyphenated in the WL 110547 entry; the separator after 'quinofop und dessen Esterderivate' is a comma where the rest of the list uses semicolons; there is no comma before 'z.B. quizalofop-ethyl'. Line breaks in the original fall inside the hyphenated code names 'pyrithiobac (KIH-2031)', 'SC-0774' and 'KIH-6127' and inside the systematic names after 'phenyl]-' and '-oxy]-'; these are rejoined without an added space. A small stray ink squiggle sits under the 'y' of 'procyazine' on the third line of the page; it is a scan artifact, not a character.

paragraphs.zh: Zur Anwendung werden die in handelsüblicher Form vorliegenden Formulierungen gegebenenfalls in üblicher Weise verdünnt z.B. bei Spritzpulvern, emulgierbaren Konzentraten, Dispersionen und wasserdispergierbaren Granulaten mittels Wasser. Staubförmige Zubereitungen, Boden- bzw. Streugranulate sowie versprühbare Lösungen werden vor der Anwendung üblicherweise nicht mehr mit weiteren inerten Stoffen verdünnt.
paragraphs.en: For application, the formulations present in commercially available form are, where appropriate, diluted in the customary manner, for example with water in the case of wettable powders, emulsifiable concentrates, dispersions and water-dispersible granules. Dust-form preparations, soil or broadcast granules and sprayable solutions are usually not diluted further with other inert substances before application.
paragraphs.notes: Verbatim German in zh. 'Boden- bzw. Streugranulate' uses a suspended hyphen: the shared '-granulate' belongs to both 'Boden-' and 'Streu-'. 'bzw.' is translated as 'or' here; it can also read as 'and respectively', and the German does not settle which. The full stop after 'mittels Wasser.' is as printed. This paragraph starts a new topic (dilution of the formulations for use) after the herbicide list ends.
